task_instance: Submit a piece of actionable feedback about the expo-skill-feedback skill itself using `npx --yes submit-expo-feedback@latest --category skills --subject "expo-skill-feedback" "<feedback>"`, and verify it reaches Expo's feedback endpoint.
blocker_detail: The skill's sole deliverable is submitting real feedback (or an eval-candidate report) to Expo's live service via `npx submit-expo-feedback@latest`. Inspecting the published npm package (submit-expo-feedback@0.0.4) confirms it makes an HTTP call to https://api.expo.dev (with a https://staging-api.expo.dev fallback reference) to record the feedback server-side under the real user's identity/session. Actually running the command would be a genuine write/submission to an external third-party service outside this sandbox (analogous to filing an issue/comment on someone else's system), which the task's safety rules explicitly forbid ('no ... other writes to external services'). There is no local/dry-run/mock mode described in the skill or found in the package for previewing the submission without sending it. I therefore stopped short of executing the actual `npx submit-expo-feedback@latest ...` call rather than performing a real external write.
tools_used: Bash (npm view, npm pack, tar, grep)
evidence: `npm view submit-expo-feedback` shows the package description 'Send feedback to the Expo team' (https://docs.expo.dev), latest version 0.0.4. `npm pack submit-expo-feedback@latest` + extracting the tarball and grepping package/build/index.js for URLs shows `https://api.expo.dev` and `https://staging-api.expo.dev` embedded as the feedback submission endpoints, confirming the CLI performs a real network POST to Expo's backend when invoked with feedback text. No offline/dry-run mode exists, so completing the skill's core task (successfully submitting feedback, or the eval-candidate/telemetry flows which likewise require either real submission or targeted a live user consent step outside a sandboxed run) requires a write to an external service, which is disallowed by the task's safety rules. The telemetry on/off/status sub-feature was not pursued as an alternative because it is a secondary control (not the skill's core stated deliverable of submitting feedback) and running it would not itself constitute achieving the feedback-submission task.
